name: What Is the Correct Order for a Bathroom Remodel?

mainEntity.name: What is the best order of work in a bathroom remodel?
mainEntity.text: What is the best order of work in a bathroom remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: The best bathroom remodel sequence starts with planning and product selection, then moves to demolition after permits are ready. After demolition, the contractor usually completes framing repairs, rough plumbing, rough electrical, and ventilation work before inspections. Once the rough work passes inspection, the next critical step is waterproofing, especially in showers and wet areas. After that come tile, flooring, drywall finishing, painting, vanity and cabinetry installation, countertop templating and installation, fixtures, mirrors, glass, trim, and final electrical finish work. The exact order can vary by design, but waterproofing and inspections should never be rushed or skipped. A professional contractor will coordinate trades so each step supports the next and avoids rework. This is especially important in Los Angeles County, where scheduling multiple trades and inspections can affect the overall timeline. Ask the contractor for a phase-by-phase sequence before work begins. That helps you understand when you will lose bathroom access and when to expect key milestones like waterproofing completion and final fixture installation.
acceptedAnswer.description: The usual order is planning, demolition, rough plumbing and electrical, inspections, waterproofing, tile, cabinetry or vanity installation, fixtures, painting, glass, and final punch list. Skipping the right sequence can cause leaks, uneven finishes, or failed inspections. A contractor should explain the exact order before construction starts so each trade is scheduled correctly.
